declared_role: defensive (secondarily diversifier) - the abstract and section 4.3 claim that when assets exhibit jump risk the skewness-based risk parity portfolio 'produce[s] better allocation than volatility-based risk parity portfolios', i.e. it avoids over-allocating to assets whose losses arrive as jumps and 'remain[s] invested in skewed assets once the jump risk has been observed' (section 6); section 5.1 frames the equity-factor application as showing that 'the size and value allocation is generally overestimated in factor-based investing, because the portfolio construction does not take into account the skewness risk'. Paper wording only; no performance was consulted.
